title: Imaging cellular activity across all organs reveals body-wide circuits.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the public Janelia S3 bucket (no login needed). The ruettenv/WHOLISTIC/ folder holds 20 objects totalling 352 GB: one functional whole-body calcium recording (f338, a single 327 GB Nikon .nd2 raw microscope file), anatomy stacks (8.1 GB and 5.9 GB two-photon .tif, 3.3 GB .czi cell-counting stack, two 1.6–1.9 GB confocal .nd2, a 4.1 GB Danionella .nd2), PNG projections and a 54 MB Blender body model. ExM/ is a 43 GB zarr volume; wSara/ is 31 GB of other expansion-microscopy raw images. No per-cell activity traces, segmentations, cell-type or organ labels, or any tables anywhere. Listed the three GitHub repos: code only. The PMC link the context script returned (PMC12973488) is an unrelated cognitive-science paper; the bioRxiv preprint (PMC12393375) data statement was read in full text.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Preprint data statement: 'Raw WHOLISTIC data will be made available' at the S3 URL; that is the only data promised. Descriptions of cell-type responses (chondrocytes to cold, meninges to ketamine, nephron waves) come from the abstract and preprint text; the Nature version's data statement was not retrievable (paywall redirect).

a1_downloadable.note: Public S3 bucket lists and serves without login; checked the listing, did not download any file (all far over the 50 MB cap).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label anywhere: no table of per-cell traces, organ or cell-type assignments, or stimulus annotations was deposited. Any target (cell type, organ, stimulus response) would have to be constructed by re-running registration, segmentation and manual annotation on raw images. Checked in the bucket listing.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs exist only as raw microscope volumes (.nd2/.tif/.czi); extracting per-cell features requires the authors' cluster-scale registration and Spark-based segmentation pipeline.

a4_units_stated.note: No tabular values exist to carry units; raw fluorescence counts only.

a5_enough_rows.note: Only one functional recording (fish f338) is public; the unit for any physiological claim is the animal, so n=1 animal. Cell count per fish not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 327 GB single raw .nd2 functional recording; 352 GB for the whole WHOLISTIC folder
a6_fits_laptop.note: Working set is ~65x the 5 GB limit and raw imaging; processing needs the authors' distributed registration/segmentation pipeline.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper describes many experiments (cold, ketamine, hypoxia, optogenetics, Danionella); the bucket has one functional recording, so the deposit does not match the paper's scope.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists; any cell-type or organ label would come from the authors' segmentation model plus manual anatomy annotation, not a direct measurement.

backbone.name: none applicable (raw light-sheet calcium imaging; no frozen-backbone fit for laptop CPU)
backbone.hardware: cluster / GPU for registration and segmentation
backbone.licence: not stated on the S3 bucket

honest_claim_h3: Not reachable: with one raw 327 GB recording and no labels, no model claim could be made on a laptop.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use whole-body calcium activity of each cell in a larval zebrafish to predict which organ or cell type it belongs to.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell activity time series from whole-body light-sheet recordings; number of cells unknown, and only one recording (one fish) is public, as a raw 327 GB file.
plain_idea.predict: The organ or tissue each cell sits in, which would have to come from manual anatomical annotation that was not deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Physiologists would learn whether activity patterns alone identify tissues, which could automate annotation of future whole-body recordings.

label_elsewhere.sources: None found; no other public whole-body pancellular calcium dataset is known to me.
label_elsewhere.why: The label would exist only in this (undeposited) annotation, so no external training or validation data.

ml_idea: Classify cell or organ identity from whole-body calcium dynamics; blocked because only one raw 327 GB recording and no traces or labels are public.

effort.compute_note: Sizes read from the S3 listing; nothing timed. Registration and segmentation of a 327 GB volume time series is cluster-scale work per the preprint methods (Spark).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the S3 bucket for any processed traces or label tables: done, none exist, so the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A5 and A6: the only public data is raw imaging (one 327 GB functional recording plus anatomy stacks) with no per-cell traces, no labels and n=1 animal; any target would need cluster-scale processing and manual annotation.
